messages:
elaine: Ran a targeted perf sweep on streaming vs non-streaming today. Short goal: identify MB sizing that keeps p99 < 600ms on A100 for vicuna-13b-q4 without tanking throughput.
noah: Nice. What were the input distributions?
elaine: Mix of short chat turns (avg tokens per turn 40) and longer completions (avg 220). Concurrency steady ~200 active clients.
diego: Which kernels and runtime?
elaine: redwood-worker v2.15, kernels: fast_attn_v3, fast_attn_v2, fallback_attention. KV cache enabled. Tests: microbatch_target sweep [2,4,8,12] and streaming flush_ms [20,40,80]. Collected p50/p95/p99, kernel usage, kv miss rate.
elaine: Results summary:
- streaming flush=20ms, mb_target=2: p50=25ms p95=120ms p99=480ms throughput=220 rps, kernels: v3:84%, v2:10%, fallback:6%, kv_miss=2.5%
- streaming flush=40ms, mb_target=8: p50=30ms p95=340ms p99=930ms throughput=560 rps, kernels: v3:68%, v2:18%, fallback:14%, kv_miss=9.1%
- buffered completions mb_target=12: p50=20ms p95=180ms p99=390ms throughput=720 rps, kernels: v3:90%, v2:7%, fallback:3%, kv_miss=1.2%
- buffered completions mb_target=4: p50=22ms p95=200ms p99=420ms throughput=460 rps, kernels similar to mb=12 but slightly higher fallback.
noah: So streaming tails blow up with larger microbatch targets and larger client buffer. Makes sense: longer incremental prefixes cause kv churn and hit fallback.
diego: Any traces from p99 samples? stack + kernel name?
elaine: Captured 12 p99 traces. Common pattern: multiple small chunks causing repeated KV lookups, then a request gets routed with partially populated KV causing fallback_attention for layers 6-8. We also saw occasional sequence-length misprediction leading kernel_selector to pick fallback.
noah: Mitigations we should try:
- prefer kernel v3 via hint for streaming paths
- enable KV prefetch on first chunk to reduce cold misses
- cap streaming mb_target to 3-4
- aggressive stream_flush reduce to 15-25ms for low-latency flows
- selective batching policy: route short-turn chat to tight cap, long completions to larger cap
elaine: Agreed. Next actions: A/B run with streaming_cap=3 + kv_prefetch on + kernel_hint=v3 vs baseline (cap=8). Collect 2h window and perf-bot will summarize.
perf-bot: Perf run scheduled: id=run-20260318-12, compare baseline vs streaming_cap3. Metrics collection starts in 5m.
diego: Bonus check: try applying kernel_hint only when avg_seq_len < 120 to avoid hurting long completions.
elaine: Good call. I'll include that rule in canary config. Posting logs/plots when finished.
